title: Revision Palimpsest
concept: A technical reply is a translucent editorial layer laid over a retained original. Five compositions move from the source/reply pair, through a stepped paper stack, into the evidence gap, a marked human-review proof, and a filed outcome. The original remains visibly separate. Missing evidence leaves a vacant reference layer and produces a clarification; a linked illustrative reference allows only a human-review draft. The typography, proof marks, paper folds and registration marks make this a document-review story rather than a network diagram.
metaphor: An editor's light table: translucent paper reveals what was inherited, added and still needs judgment.
choreography: The retained original settles first; the vendor reply floats over it, and an editorial underline questions an unsupported pointer.
Source, vendor reply and draft enter as three staggered document layers, making provenance visible at a glance.
The evidence layer is either an empty dashed footprint or a printed reference fragment; the visible next action changes with that state.
Original and working proof open side by side. A finite pencil movement accompanies the marked evidence or applicability question for human review.
The original settles into a folder and the clarification or review draft slides alongside it; the history remains visible.
interaction: The host's missing/linked evidence choice changes phase 2 from an empty reference footprint and Ask for evidence to a linked reference fragment and Draft for review. The same choice carries into human review and the final filed result. Base defaults conservatively to missing.
contributions: Translucent physical layers preserve source, reply and draft identity without small dashboard cards.
An evidence footprint changes the actual page content and next action, while preserving the human-judgment boundary.
Finite paper, ink and proof-mark choreography has fully informative static and reduced-motion states and authored English/Korean text.
limitations: All diagram data, references, review marks and outcomes are illustrative, not performed engineering. A linked reference does not establish applicability or approval. No real vendor record, provenance verification, issued clarification or final human decision is represented. This entry provides authored SVG/CSS, not evidence of actual mobile-device acceptance.
